cases.event: One autumn, the fictional solar panels at {E} produced much less power than usual.
cases.q: What most likely caused the panels at {E} to produce less power?
restate: The panels at {E} produced less power than usual, and the question asks why.
Something caused the solar panels at {E} to produce less power one autumn.
cases.answer: Dust from a nearby road project most likely caused the panels at {E} to produce less power, because it blocked sunlight from the cells.
cases.sum: the evidence points to the dust from the road project as the reason the panels produced less power.
cases.myth: The panels at {E} produced less power because autumn sunlight carries no energy at all.
cases.mythClause: only the panels painted with a logo lost power
cases.altText: Some visitors suggested that the solar cells at {E} had simply worn out.
cases.patternQ: What pattern connects the road project and the power produced at {E}?
cases.patternA: Power dropped while dust from the road project coated the panels and returned to normal after the panels were washed, so the power followed the dust.
cases.patternSum: the power output fell and rose with the amount of dust on the panels.

obs.text: A road crew began digging next to {E}, and power output dropped by about {n0} percent that same week.
obs.tag: the drop during the road work
exps: the drop began exactly when the digging started, which points to the road project
a drop that sudden lines up with the start of the road work, not with slow aging
the timing ties the lost power to something new happening beside the farm

obs.text: Workers found a gray layer of dust covering the glass of the panels.
exps: dust on the glass blocks sunlight, so less light reaches the cells to make power
this shows how the road project could cut the power, since covered panels receive less light

obs.text: Within {n1} days after the panels were washed, their power output returned to normal.
exps: the power came back as soon as the dust was removed, which is what would happen if dust were the cause
removing the dust removed the problem, so the two are linked
once the cause was cleaned away, the effect disappeared

obs.text: Panels installed only last year lost just as much power as panels installed ten years ago.
exps: worn-out cells would affect old panels far more than new ones, but both lost the same amount
this rules out wear, because brand-new cells had no time to wear out
if aging were the cause, the newest panels would have held up better
predExps: if only the oldest panels were at risk, the new ones would have kept their power, but they did not
this directly contradicts the prediction, since age made no difference
the prediction expected an age difference that never appeared
